correctness.rationale: For recursive trees grown by independent uniform parents and n>=2, let L=leaf count and W=unordered-pair distance sum, A=sum of distance centralities of leaves. For a fixed size-m tree, adding a child at uniform parent P gives L’=L+1-J and W’=W+m+S(P), J=1_{P leaf}. The leaf-centrality update yields E(W_(m+1)-A_(m+1)|T_m)=W_m-A_m-(1-1/m)L_m. With E L_m=m/2 this telescopes to E(W_m-A_m)=-(m-1)(m-2)/4. Total covariance of L’,W’ gives C_(m+1)=(m+1)C_m/m-(m-1)(m-2)/(4m), C2=0; summing yields C_n=nH_n-(n²+5n-2)/4, 0 at n2/3 and strictly negative n>=4. Independently enumerated all recursive parent lists for n2..8 (5040 trees at n8) and computed W by BFS pair distances, confirming mean identity and exact covariance. The optional scaled-correlation constant follows from established Neininger 2002 Wiener variance (31-3π²)n^4/18 and Var L=n/12. Finite enumeration corroborates, the recurrence proves all n.
residual_risks: Finite tests cannot prove all-parameter claim; proof reconstruction establishes stated scope.

originality.rationale: Neininger 2002 Theorem 1.2 treats the Wiener index jointly with INTERNAL PATH LENGTH, not leaf count; its full 11-page source was read through authorized institutional access. Grübel–Michailow 2014 treats Wiener asymptotics via boundary theory, not this mixed leaf centrality. The exact mixed covariance is not present in those examined claims.

The optional correlation constant uses a published Wiener variance rather than independently re-proving that asymptotic.
